expectations.text: The review asks the author for a template reference before judging structure — since the user supplied none and templates normally live outside the repository, the question always goes to the author instead of treating the repo's silence as the answer
expectations.evidence: Question 1 of 'O que precisa de você': 'Existe um template de design doc no time? Templates normalmente moram no wiki ou no drive, não no repositório — o que eu vejo aqui é pista, não resposta.'

expectations.text: Structural additions are framed as suggestions from the skill's default catalog, not imposed as requirements, since no template governs the document
expectations.evidence: Opening paragraph: 'segui o catálogo padrão de seções, e por isso as sugestões estruturais abaixo são sugestões, não exigências'; the two extra sections (Testabilidade e observabilidade, Perguntas em aberto) are offered with 'não há template governando, então são sugestões'.

expectations.text: The reply separates findings into questions for the author versus edits applied
expectations.evidence: Two explicit headings: '## O que já apliquei' (6 numbered edits) and '## O que precisa de você' (10 numbered questions).

expectations.text: Missing trade-offs and alternatives become questions to the author — the edited doc gains no fabricated cons, alternatives, or metrics
expectations.evidence: Questions 4 and 5 ask for the accepted costs and the alternatives incl. 'não fazer nada'; the edited fanout-de-notificacoes.md contains no Trade-offs and no Alternativas section and no new numbers — candidate cons are listed only in the reply, as prompts for the author.

expectations.text: A glossary is added or suggested at the BEGINNING of the document covering DLQ, TPS, CDC and SLA
expectations.evidence: '## Glossário' was inserted directly after the header table and before 'Visão geral', with entries for CDC, DLQ, Exchange, Fanout, In-app, Provider, SLA, TPS, Worker.

expectations.text: The mermaid diagram is now followed by explanatory text
expectations.evidence: The author's orphan Mermaid flowchart was replaced by a validated C4 container SVG (67 KB at docs/design/diagrams/arquitetura-fanout.svg) with the DSL folded in <details>, and is followed by a paragraph explaining CDC → dispatcher → exchange → per-channel queues/workers → DLQ and TPS control.

expectations.text: The out-of-scope items are no longer mere negations of goals (rewritten honestly or turned into a question)
expectations.evidence: The doc still shows the original two negations, but the assertion allows the question path: reply item 3 states 'Fora de escopo não exclui nada … são a negação dos objetivos' and asks the author what genuinely falls outside, offering candidates rather than inventing exclusions.

expectations.text: Vague goals ('melhorar a performance', 'garantir o SLA') are flagged as unmeasurable and the author is asked for numbers — no invented targets
expectations.evidence: Reply item 2 quotes the three goals, calls them uncheckable and asks for the SLA number, current slowness and expected peak; the doc's '## Objetivos' section is left verbatim ('Deixei os objetivos como estavam').

expectations.text: The edited document remains in Portuguese and preserves the author's structure and voice
expectations.evidence: All added prose is Portuguese; original sections (Visão geral, Objetivos, Fora de escopo, Solução, Plano) and their order are kept, with only Glossário and Escopo e contexto inserted; the DSL reproduces exactly the author's elements and edges, including in-app having no DLQ.

expectations.text: The header is honestly refreshed (Última atualização set to the real current date)
expectations.evidence: Header row now reads '**Última atualização** | 2026-07-20', which matches the real date (`date +%Y-%m-%d` recorded in the transcript notes); Estado stayed 'Em revisão' and was raised as question 10 instead of being changed unilaterally.
